topic:
Sharp all-regime recovery of the population CATE law with unrestricted high-dimensional discrete confounders. Observe n iid (X,A,Y), X in [d], binary A and Y, under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and known fixed overlap epsilon in (0,1/2). Cell masses are arbitrary and unknown; propensities and both outcome regressions are unknown, with no smoothness, positive mass floor, effect separation, or exclusion of ties. The target G_P=sum_{x:p_x>0} p_x delta_(mu_1x-mu_0x) is the population law of conditional mean effects. Determine, up to epsilon-only constants and uniformly over n>=1,d>=2, inf_Ghat sup_P E[W1(Ghat,G_P)^2]. Construct one explicit computable probability-valued estimator and a matching all-estimator converse, deriving consistency and parametric-risk boundaries; leave the exact rate open. The full sparse-to-dense frontier is the kernel: a dense-regime theorem alone, a scalar-functional collection, or a one-sided bound is insufficient. Novelty must survive Vinayak-Kong-Kakade paired-binomial change-law estimation and Lee-Bacak-Kennedy fixed heterogeneous trial counts by handling unknown mass-weighted observational sampling. Consumer: categorical-profile CATE-distribution analyses motivated by Mizuguchi-Sawamura's dexamethasone/PONV study. This does not identify individual potential-outcome differences or validate zero-atom claims from W1 alone. Delegate estimator algebra and tuning, retaining the original law class. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A separated-atom hypercube keeps the observed experiments close while moving the CATE law in Wasserstein distance. Together with a total cellwise plug-in construction, the presolve reports a matching risk of order d/n when n is at least d cubed, on the original unrestricted model. An independently checked eight-cell instance has positive probabilities, exact neighboring transport cost 1/512, and n-sample KL approximately 0.063. This shows why the scalar optimal-value rate cannot simply be transplanted. A mass-weighted Lipschitz extension and a deterministic positive grouped moment-reconstruction certificate provide a route beyond this regime. Paired-binomial law recovery and fixed heterogeneous trial-count estimation are existing precedents; grouping alone is not novelty. These derivations and comparisons require independent verification.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Control and optimize the joint moment-estimation process uniformly over all Lipschitz test functions under arbitrary unknown cell masses and propensities, and prove a matching converse in the remaining sample-size/category regimes. The dense result alone does not complete the promised paper.
EARLY KILL TEST: Test the proposed joint reconstruction certificate, with exact factorial covariances, on the explicit separated-atom hypercube and on two effect clusters with unknown unequal masses and propensities at both overlap boundaries. It must respect the d/n dense lower bound and deliver a concrete nontrivial clustered bound without known-weight assumptions or discarded null cells; a contradictory scalar-rate certificate must be abandoned, and an affirmative exact-class generic collision or obstruction should stop or pivot the run.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_discrete_cate_law_wasserstein_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp all-regime minimax squared-Wasserstein risk for the population-weighted categorical CATE law when cell masses, propensities, and both outcome regressions are unknown.

source_refs.claim: Derives minimax rates for the scalar ATE with high-dimensional discrete confounders, but not recovery of the population CATE law.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: Establishes Wasserstein recovery of a paired-binomial change distribution with a fixed common number of trials per latent pair.
source_refs.author: Ramya Korlakai Vinayak, Weihao Kong, Sham M. Kakade

source_refs.claim: Studies smooth binomial mixing densities with observed heterogeneous trial counts, while leaving their minimax rates open.
source_refs.author: JungHo Lee, Valerio Baćak, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.excerpt: The bound permits unknown unequal propensities, arbitrary occupied-cell masses, null cells
the extension always returns a positive real probability measure

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing population-of-parameters results condition on fixed entities with fixed or observed trial counts, whereas each observational cell has a random multinomial count, an unknown propensity-controlled treatment split, and an unknown mass that also weights the target. The banked Jackson-factorial construction handles one scalar functional; it neither produces a compatible positive moment sequence nor controls all mass-weighted Lipschitz transforms simultaneously. Its lower priors can also separate a scalar mean while failing to separate laws in W1. The first proof step that must change is the scalar localized polynomial certificate: it must become a joint treated-control factorial-moment certificate followed by positive-measure reconstruction and uniform Lipschitz-test control.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving a rate r(n,d,epsilon) and constants c_epsilon,C_epsilon such that c_epsilon r is at most and C_epsilon r is at least the all-estimator minimax W1-squared risk for every n≥1 and d≥2, with a computable probability-valued attaining estimator and exact consistency and parametric-risk regions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its sparse-to-dense treatment of unrestricted categorical confounding provides the closest motivation and phase-diagram structure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Categorical adjustment creates many sparsely sampled cells -> ordinary cellwise causal estimators lose uniform validity -> scalar ATE theory reveals collision-driven phase transitions -> recovering the full population CATE law requires a new all-regime frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a bivariate mixing law and push it through the difference map, paired with moment-based information-theoretic lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is also a distribution of differences between two latent Bernoulli means, but fixed paired trials must be replaced by random mass-weighted observational cells.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize by empirical count scale, estimate factorial moments, repair them through a feasible moment program, and prove Wasserstein risk using polynomial approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies positive-measure reconstruction machinery; the new proof requires joint treated-control moments with unknown weights and propensities.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine localized fuzzy-hypotheses lower bounds with higher-order causal estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its oracle-versus-nuisance decomposition is a natural template for proving why full-law recovery cannot inherit the scalar ATE rate.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest finite-sample confidence sets for the unrestricted categorical population CATE law whose W1 diameter matches the all-regime minimax estimation radius despite null cells and effect ties.

source_refs.claim: Develops confidence bands for sorted effects under regularity conditions that do not cover arbitrary atomic ties.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Iván Fernández-Val, Ye Luo

source_refs.claim: Constructs exact pointwise CDF and quantile intervals for a fixed-trial one-parameter binomial mixing distribution.
source_refs.author: Pallavi Basu, Barak Brill, Daniel Yekutieli
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics

source_refs.excerpt: The direct selected-factorial tail certificate and heavy Gaussian/fallback radius could not be proved
Coverage and root-n W1-diameter are uniform over every collision, merge, and split stratum

open_problems.why_unsolved: Sorted-effect inference typically uses no-tie or positive-density assumptions, while this law is intrinsically atomic and permits arbitrary collisions. The accepted proxy-law construction is fixed-dimensional and Lipschitz in finitely many summaries, but growing-category recovery would use pilot-selected, increasing-order factorial moments with random cell intensities. The downgraded scalar ATE run could not prove a direct tail certificate even for one selected aggregate. Law-valued inference additionally requires simultaneous control over all Lipschitz tests and inversion into a nonempty positive-measure set without a cellwise union bound or an unjustified square-root-of-MSE conversion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit random set C_n of probability measures satisfying uniform coverage at least 1-alpha and worst-case expected W1 diameter comparable to the minimax estimation radius in every n,d regime, together with a matching lower bound for every honest confidence set.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates reporting a full effect distribution rather than an average and makes simultaneous uncertainty central to the scientific use of heterogeneity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects conceal heterogeneity -> sorted effects expose the population distribution -> useful heterogeneity summaries require simultaneous uncertainty -> atomic ties and sparse observational cells require honest Wasserstein confidence sets

method_exemplars.technique: Invert finite-sample composite tests for mixing-distribution CDF and quantile constraints using stochastic monotonicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides assumption-light inference for a latent binomial mixing law; the causal extension must instead invert constraints from a joint observational cell likelihood.

method_exemplars.technique: Use dual optimal-transport geometry and debiased estimation for confidence intervals involving latent mixing measures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired diameter is a Wasserstein functional of a latent law, but here the observation operator has unknown causal weights and random arm counts.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the minimax detectability of a positive population mass of exact CATE nonresponders, including uniform impossibility without separation and a sharp separated-alternative boundary.

source_refs.claim: Interprets a CATE distribution peaked near zero as evidence of possible dexamethasone nonresponders while acknowledging that true CATEs are unobservable.
source_refs.author: Taisuke Mizuguchi, Shigehito Sawamura

source_refs.claim: Explains why estimating a mixing distribution does not directly estimate a distinguished null atom and develops separate null-proportion machinery.
source_refs.author: Xiangjie Xue, Yong Wang
source_refs.venue: Australian & New Zealand Journal of Statistics

source_refs.claim: Shows that fixed-size binomial mixtures identify only finitely many moments of an unrestricted mixing distribution.
source_refs.author: Graham R. Wood

open_problems.why_unsolved: The map G to G({0}) is discontinuous in W1 because zero mass can be moved to arbitrarily nearby nonzero effects at arbitrarily small transport cost. Consequently, W1-consistent law estimation cannot validate an exact nonresponder claim. The observational experiment adds two separately noisy Bernoulli means, unknown cell weights, and random arm counts. Existing null-proportion warnings do not give a categorical causal testing frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An impossibility theorem for uniformly testing positive zero-atom mass on the unrestricted class, followed by matching sample-complexity upper and lower bounds for testing G_P({0})≥rho against alternatives excluding effects from (-gamma,gamma), as a function of n,d,epsilon,rho,gamma.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the concrete clinical nonresponder interpretation and states that the underlying CATE ground truth is unavailable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PONV prophylaxis may help only some patients -> fitted CATE histograms peak near zero -> the peak is interpreted as nonresponse despite unobservable true effects -> exact nonresponder mass requires separation-aware inference

method_exemplars.technique: Separate estimation of a distinguished null atom from nonparametric recovery of the remaining mixing distribution, with explicit identifiability regularization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems concern mass at a special zero point rather than weak recovery of the whole distribution.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact tests of binomial-mixture distribution constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Test inversion can support the separated upper bound after the direct mixture likelihood is replaced by the joint treated-control cell experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the localized and adaptive minimax W1-squared frontier when the categorical CATE law lies within radius sigma of an unknown point mass, uniformly through effect ties and cluster merges and without knowing sigma.

source_refs.excerpt: The shrinking-radius wedge remains open because the available radius channel gives a product-type separation
Add an adaptive-radius extension or a lower bound showing the price of adaptation to unknown sigma
effects unresolved at the rho scale are pooled

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked scalar ATE converse leaves a shrinking-radius wedge because its hypothesis-independent channel gives product-type rather than minimum-type separation. For a law target, decreasing spread also changes the transport geometry: nearby atoms merge and their labels become unstable although aggregate mass may remain estimable. The first proof step that changes is the radius-indexed lower construction, which must separate complete effect laws in W1 while keeping their unknown-weight observational experiments close; the upper construction must adapt its localization without knowing the cluster radius.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A localized minimax theorem for laws satisfying inf_c max_{x:p_x>0}|mu_1x-mu_0x-c|≤sigma with rate r(n,d,sigma), plus either one sigma-adaptive estimator attaining it for all sigma or a testing lower bound quantifying the unavoidable adaptation penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its collision-based framing distinguishes unstable labeled effects from a stable quotient effect law.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Heterogeneous effects define a latent law -> labels and weights destabilize when effects collide -> Wasserstein aggregation remains meaningful through collisions -> seek an adaptive spread-localized CATE-law frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate polynomial effect moments and aggregate cluster masses rather than separated labels, measuring error through Wasserstein-stable merges.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested theorem must remain stable as effect atoms merge, making collision-aware aggregation more appropriate than eigengap-dependent labeled recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize before polynomial approximation and use moment-matched alternatives near a nonsmooth diagonal.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An unknown point-mass center creates a moving nonsmooth diagonal whose localization must account for causal arm ratios and effect clusters.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the joint minimax phase diagram for recovery of the original population CATE law when the overlap bound epsilon_n may vanish, without trimming or changing the target population.

source_refs.claim: Fixes propensities inside [epsilon,1-epsilon], leaving the interaction between categorical sparsity and vanishing overlap unresolved for law recovery.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: Reviews weak-positivity remedies whose stabilization commonly comes from changing the estimand toward an overlap population.
source_refs.author: Roland A. Matsouaka, Yunji Zhou

source_refs.excerpt: The proof program does not address deteriorating overlap
For every fixed 0<epsilon<1/2, there is C_epsilon<infinity

open_problems.why_unsolved: For the original population law, trimming or overlap weighting changes the target masses. Existing categorical constructions freeze overlap before setting polynomial degrees and variance bounds. When epsilon_n vanishes, the arm-specific intensities n p_x e_x and n p_x(1-e_x) can lie in different sparsity regimes, and inverse-propensity factors amplify high factorial moments. A lower bound must jointly vary masses and propensities while retaining valid causal laws, so replacing n by n epsilon_n in a fixed-overlap formula is not justified.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching rate r(n,d,epsilon_n) for squared-W1 loss, attained by a computable estimator of the untrimmed population law, with explicit consistency and parametric-risk conditions across category-sparse, arm-sparse, and ordinary-noise regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly separates instability caused by extreme propensities from remedies that redefine the target population.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Extreme propensities create unstable inverse weights -> trimming and overlap weighting restore stability -> those remedies alter the target population -> preserving the original population CATE law requires a weak-overlap minimax frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Poissonize categorical counts, split rare and common cells, and prove collision-based causal minimax lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same occupancy experiment remains, but every treated-control moment and indistinguishability calculation must track epsilon_n explicitly.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze heterogeneous binomial trial counts through effective-information and bias-variance decompositions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Vanishing propensities induce highly heterogeneous arm-specific counts; the new step is allowing those counts to be random and coupled to unknown masses.

open_problems.open_problem: Under a marginal sensitivity model for hidden confounding, characterize and estimate the sharp identified set of population CATE laws over high-dimensional categorical profiles in Hausdorff-Wasserstein distance.

source_refs.claim: Derives bounds on individual CATEs and the scalar ATE under bounded treatment-selection odds, but not the jointly attainable population law.
source_refs.author: Steve Yadlowsky, Hongseok Namkoong, Sanjay Basu, John Duchi, Lu Tian

source_refs.claim: Constructs sharp functional intervals for CATE under violations of unconfoundedness, but not a law-valued identified set.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Angela Zhou

source_refs.claim: Provides doubly valid and doubly sharp inference for scalar ATE sensitivity bounds.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn, Kevin Guo, Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pointwise intervals for each categorical CATE do not establish which simultaneous effect selections can arise from one full-data law, nor do they quantify the pushforward-law uncertainty created by unknown cell masses. Law-level sharpness must account for compatibility across treatment arms, and estimation must combine sensitivity-bound nuisances with sparse multinomial occupancy. The located literature treats pointwise CATE or scalar ATE sensitivity, not Hausdorff-W1 recovery of the attainable law set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp characterization of the set of attainable measures sum_x p_x delta_(tau_x), together with a computable set estimator and matching upper and lower rates for expected Hausdorff-W1 loss.

writing_exemplar.why: It turns the unverifiability of exchangeability into a precise conditional-effect sensitivity problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational CATEs require untestable exchangeability -> bounded hidden selection yields intervals rather than point identification -> pointwise bounds support robust personalized conclusions -> population heterogeneity requires the jointly attainable law

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize conditional means over bounded likelihood ratios and prove sharpness through extremal reweighting constructions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cellwise extremal laws are the natural ingredients for proving law-level compatibility and sharpness.

method_exemplars.technique: Use distributionally robust duality and orthogonal scores to obtain doubly sharp and doubly valid bound estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired set estimator needs analogous robustness uniformly over Lipschitz transforms and sparse categorical cells.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the two-sample minimax Wasserstein rate for a transported population CATE law when causal outcomes are observed in a source sample and categorical target-population masses are learned from a separate unlabeled sample.

source_refs.claim: Derives efficient and locally minimax estimators for transported scalar ATEs under source-target covariate shift, not for a target-population CATE law.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Edward H. Kennedy, Lisa M. Bodnar, Ashley I. Naimi

source_refs.claim: Notes that many-valued discrete effect modifiers can leave inadequate observations at individual covariate levels even in large studies.
source_refs.author: Issa J. Dahabreh and collaborators

open_problems.why_unsolved: A transported law couples two occupancy processes: source cells determine noisy effect locations while target cells determine their population masses. Empty source-only and target-only categories create a two-sample collision boundary, and density-ratio formulations may be undefined on rare categories. Existing transport theory concentrates on averages or regular low-dimensional CATE functions; the located literature does not characterize minimax W1 recovery of this law-valued target.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp rate r(n_source,n_target,d,epsilon) for estimating the target-weighted CATE law, with a computable probability-valued estimator, a matching two-sample lower bound, and necessary-and-sufficient consistency conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates causal information learned in a source population from weighting information learned in a target population.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Study and decision populations can differ -> effect modification invalidates source-only summaries -> transport reweights source causal information to target covariates -> reporting full heterogeneity requires transporting the CATE law rather than only its mean

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a transport identifying functional, orthogonal score, efficiency bound, and higher-order minimax correction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the source-target decomposition; the changed step is replacing one linear functional by uniform estimation over Lipschitz transforms of CATE.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover a distribution of latent parameter differences by estimating a joint mixing law and pushing it forward.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transported target remains a weighted law of differences, but its weights come from an independent target sample rather than a fixed entity population.

literature_map:
Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, arXiv:2405.00118) give the closest causal experiment: unrestricted high-dimensional discrete confounders, but only scalar ATE rates.
Tian, Kong, and Valiant (NeurIPS 2017, arXiv:1709.02707) recover a population of binomial parameters in earth-mover distance with fixed homogeneous trials.
Vinayak, Kong, Valiant, and Kakade (ICML 2019, arXiv:1902.04553) show that the binomial-mixture NPMLE is minimax across sparse fixed-trial regimes.
Vinayak, Kong, and Kakade (2019, arXiv:1911.12568) recover a paired-binomial change distribution, the closest noncausal analogue of a CATE law.
Lee, Baćak, and Kennedy (2025, arXiv:2507.23140) allow heterogeneous observed trial counts but impose smooth mixing densities and leave their minimax rates open.
Han, Jiao, and Weissman (COLT 2018, arXiv:1802.08405) provide local moment matching and positive-measure Wasserstein reconstruction for unlabeled distributions.
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (Annals of Statistics 2024, DOI:10.1214/24-AOS2369) develop minimax CATE-function theory under Hölder smoothness, not unrestricted categorical law recovery.
Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, and Luo (Econometrica 2018, DOI:10.3982/ECTA14415) establish sorted-effect inference, but their regular sorting theory does not cover arbitrary atomic ties.
Kallus (Management Science 2023, DOI:10.1287/mnsc.2023.4819) uses the CATE distribution for treatment-risk bounds while assuming regularity at relevant quantiles.
Basu, Brill, and Yekutieli (JCGS 2026, arXiv:2311.14424) give exact pointwise inference for fixed-trial binomial mixing distributions, not observational CATE laws.
Zeng, Kennedy, Bodnar, and Naimi (2023, arXiv:2302.00092) derive transport results for scalar ATEs, leaving transported CATE laws untreated.
Yadlowsky, Namkoong, Basu, Duchi, and Tian (Annals of Statistics 2022, DOI:10.1214/22-AOS2195) give pointwise CATE and scalar ATE sensitivity bounds, not a jointly attainable law.
Xue and Wang (ANZJS 2023, DOI:10.1111/anzs.12383) show why weak recovery of a mixing distribution does not automatically recover a distinguished null atom.
Mizuguchi and Sawamura (Scientific Reports 2023, DOI:10.1038/s41598-023-34505-0) report a near-zero dexamethasone CATE peak while acknowledging that true CATEs are unobservable.
No located source occupies the exact combination of unknown population masses, unknown propensities, two noisy outcome regressions, unrestricted atomic effects, and all-regime squared-W1 recovery.
